The LEAF platform is built using PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor (PHP) technology, Go Programming Language, and uses MySQL (Structured Query Language) as its data store within FedRAMP authorized Cloud Service Providers (CSPs). The platform is currently deployed with the VA Enterprise Cloud (VAEC) and uses VA Platform One containerization technology based on Open Container Initiative (OCI) compliant engines such as Red Hat OpenShift. The platform’s login infrastructure is integrated with the VA Active Directory to provide a unique seamless user authentication mechanism using a combination of Windows Authentication, Client Certificates, and OAuth 2.0 providers such as Microsoft Entra ID. The LEAF platform leverages observability tools using log parsing and process analysis tools such as Dynatrace to monitor system health metrics. The platform uses a representational state transfer (REST) style application program interface (API) for interfacing with other websites or applications, and JavaScript is used extensively on the client side to drive a Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) 5 and Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) based user interface. The platform’s automated test suite utilizes Go testing and benchmarking conventions, as well as Microsoft Playwright for end-to-end testing.

The VA Light Electronic Action Framework (LEAF) is a highly adaptable VA-owned and developed process improvement software that enables VA employees to rapidly digitize existing business processes. LEAF’s source code is owned by VA and soley leverages open-source software within its technology stack. Today, LEAF is a mature, operational product that has an active monthly user base of over 250,000 internal VA employees and manages over 7,000,000 VA business transactions annually. The platform helps VA medical centers, program offices, and project teams process simple requests (e.g., approval to travel), complex needs (e.g. Full Time Equivalent (FTE) backfills), and is flexible enough to be applied to any set of business processes. The LEAF Platform is based on two web application components that operate in tandem, the Request Portal and Nexus Applications. The Request Portal enables VA staff to create forms, design workflows, and identify process-specific user groups, while the Nexus enables VA medical facilities and program offices to centrally manage groups and optionally utilize a GUI-driven organizational chart. The Request Portal utilizes data from the Nexus for added utility, such as “smart” routing based on organizational hierarchy
